title: Introduce holistic load synthesizer and regression gatekeeper for perf canaries
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a configurable load synthesizer service and a regression gatekeeper component for perf canaries. New e2e tests and dashboards. No breaking API changes.
description:
Motivation: Our existing perf canary system runs historical traffic replays and a small set of synthetic probes but has gaps when real-world traffic mixes burstiness, sequence-length skew, and multi-tenant interference. This PR introduces two complementary pieces: (1) a holistic load synthesizer that can generate multi-dimensional synthetic workloads (sequence length, token distributions, client concurrency, burst shapes, KV-cache-warm patterns) and (2) a regression gatekeeper that integrates with the perf-canary pipeline to decide whether a detected signal should block a rollout based on traffic-aware statistical isolation and stratified significance checks.

Design summary: The load synthesizer is implemented as a small Go service (benchmarks/load-synth/) with a YAML-driven profile format. Profiles combine primitive generators (poisson/constrained-bursts, seq-length histograms, prompt variants) and allow composition across multiple virtual clients. The gatekeeper lives in perf-canary/controller/ and receives both baseline and candidate samples; it performs stratified bootstrap resampling per-traffic-slice (by region, seq-length bucket, and model_variant) and applies an adaptive false-discovery controller to make a binary decision with an explainability payload (top contributing slices and confidence).

What changed (high level): added load-synth executable, profile schema, CLI and local-mode; integration hook in perf-canary to trigger synth profiles as part of pre-rollout probes; a new statistical engine for stratified resampling and the gatekeeper API; dashboard tiles in observability-pack for synthesized vs real traffic comparisons; a deterministic test harness under perf-canary/tests/ that seeds RNGs to remove flakiness.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement load synthesizer service and YAML schema
- [x] Add gatekeeper component + controller integration
- [x] End-to-end deterministic tests and CI job
- [x] Observability dashboards and sample alert rules
- [x] Docs: quickstart and profile examples under redwood-docs/perf/

Why this is safe: All new components are opt-in behind a feature flag (perf.synth.enabled) and default canary pipelines are unchanged unless a profile is attached. Gatekeeper decisions are configurable (fail-blocking, advisory-only, audit-only) to allow gradual adoption.

Notes for reviewers: pay attention to the stratified bootstrap implementation for performance (we use reservoir sampling + per-slice spool to bound memory) and the CLI semantics for profile composition. The PR contains a smoke script that reproduces the sample dashboard in CI artifacts for validation.
